breakdown.description: The prompt sets the free-end rotation to zero, even though a cantilever’s free end is generally free to rotate under an end point load.
breakdown.reason: The generated specification correctly applies boundary conditions at the fixed end (slope = 0 and deflection = 0 at x = 0), and calculates the free-end slope as θ(L) = PL²/(2EI), which is non-zero. This correctly treats the free end as free to rotate, resolving the inconsistency of setting free-end rotation to zero.

breakdown.description: The prompt treats the bending moment as constant and equal to P L over the entire span, even though the cantilever moment varies linearly from the free end to the fixed end.
breakdown.reason: The generated specification explicitly states M(x) = -P(L-x), which is a linearly varying bending moment along the span. This correctly replaces the flawed assumption of a constant moment PL over the full span, and the resulting deflection formula PL³/(3EI) confirms the correct linear moment distribution was used.
